highres-TA run comparison

Six quantile-ensemble runs of the surface total alkalinity (TA) reconstruction in models/, compared on held-out bottle data, the shared test block, salinity sensitivity, time-series stations and ensemble composition. Errors are predicted minus observed, in µmol kg⁻¹. Data extracted 2026-11-10.

Overview Held-out comparison Error map Salinity sensitivity Stations Test block & uncertainty Ensemble & features

The runs

Each run changes one thing from its predecessor. The two Split-HPO runs use the older design (seven separate Optuna studies per split); the four Rashomon runs use one study per split and pick seven diverse near-best trials.

Read this before comparing headline numbers. The runs do not share one test set. A and B/C use GLODAP only (3,891 and 4,139 test rows); D, E and F add CARIMED Mediterranean bottles, which changes the block partition (4,314 test rows, only 332 shared with C). The Held-out comparison tab fixes this by scoring every row with the members that never trained on it (test block plus out-of-fold validation), so C, D, E and F are compared on identical rows.

What each model gets right and where it breaks

Limitations shared by every run

  • Intervals are too narrow. The nominal 80 % q10–q90 interval covers 69–75 % of held-out observations in every run; coastal and Southern Ocean rows of the in-situ models drop to 64–68 %.
  • Coastal water is 3× harder. Rows with bottom depth < 500 m have RMSE 45–47 (in-situ models) vs 15–20 offshore; with gridded salinity the coastal RMSE is 75–95.
  • Fresh water and high latitudes. Below salinity 30 the in-situ models reach RMSE 73–78; ≥ 60° is the worst latitude band for every model.
  • Period effects. 2000–2009 and the 1980s carry the largest errors in all runs; 1985–1994 is the easiest period.
  • Gridded salinity dominates map error. Moving from in-situ to gridded salinity roughly doubles RMSE for every model, and no feature-engineering change so far (stacked vs multi-product) closes that gap.

Held-out comparison on identical rows

Every observation is predicted only by members that never saw it: the test block by all 42 members, every other row by the 7 members of the split that held it out for validation (median across members). For the in-situ models the stacked variant swaps in the gridded salinity stack (CCI → SODA → multi-obs), which is what those models see when producing maps. That variant, not the in-situ one, is the fair comparison with E and F.

Where each model errs

Sensitivity to the salinity input

The validation runner re-predicts each row after replacing salinity with a gridded product, on the same rows. For the in-situ models this measures the error the maps inherit; for E and F the model was trained on the stack, so the stacked bar is its native input and the in-situ bar is the mismatch. Regions follow the validation definitions: coastal means bottom depth < 500 m, and the latitude split is at |lat| = 60°.

Added error vs size of the salinity mismatch (test block)

RMSE with the product minus RMSE with in-situ salinity, binned by |Sproduct − Sreference|. The reference is in-situ salinity for C and D but the stack for E and F, so for E and F the stacked product has no mismatch; pick another product to compare them. A model that is robust to salinity errors stays low on the right.

Independent time-series stations

Surface bottles from 20 stations, predicted with gridded T/S (what the maps see) and with the in-situ T/S. Station evaluation exists for C, D and E. F has not been evaluated yet: the cached station collocations in data/time_series/ lack the sss_cci and salt_soda columns, so evaluate_stations.py --stage evaluate fails until the stations are re-collocated.

Where member disagreement comes from

Mean variance across test rows, split into the data-split term and the HPO/Rashomon term (law of total variance), per quantile. Units (µmol kg⁻¹)².

Ensemble composition and feature reliance

For the Rashomon runs (C–F): CatBoost feature importance of the residual model (mean over members), how often each feature is dropped by the selected members, and the spread of selected hyperparameters. The Split-HPO runs did not store per-member trial metadata.

Rashomon set size per split

Sources: models/<run>/ensemble_test_metrics.json, validation/{predictions.parquet, scores.csv, salinity_penalty.csv}, stations/{scores.csv, predictions.parquet}, models/*.json, feature_importance/summary.csv. Held-out predictions use median aggregation (validation.yaml); the test-block table uses the saved mean aggregation. Basins are coarse boxes: Mediterranean 30–46° N, 5.5° W–37° E; Southern Ocean south of 35° S; Arctic/subpolar N north of 60° N; Indian 20–120° E north of 35° S and south of 30° N; Atlantic 70° W–20° E; Pacific otherwise.
